title: Jake Marshall Wins 2026 US Open of Surfing
htmlContent:
Marshall secured the win in Huntington Beach with a final heat score of 14.77, defeating Kanoa Igarashi, who finished with a score of 14.07, in the men's final. Throughout every round of the event, he demonstrated the confidence, power and composure that have defined his career, saving one of his strongest performances for the moment it mattered most. From his opening heat to the final horn, Marshall surfed with a clarity and purpose that left little doubt about who deserved to be standing atop the podium when the competition came to a close.

A Milestone Years in the Making

For Marshall, who grew up surfing in Southern California and has been part of the Hurley family since his days as a young competitor, the victory represents far more than another result. It is the culmination of years of dedication, resilience and an unwavering belief in what was possible. Long before this week's contest, Marshall built the foundation for this moment through countless early mornings in the water, steady improvement across every stage of his career, and a willingness to push himself even when progress was slow. Friday's win is proof that the work behind the scenes was never wasted.

A Hometown Celebration

Surrounded by family, friends, teammates and thousands of fans gathered along the Huntington Beach shoreline, Marshall claimed the event title in a defining moment for both his career and the Hurley family. The energy on the sand mirrored the intensity in the water, with the crowd erupting as the final scores were posted. For an athlete who came up through the same stretch of coastline hosting the event, lifting the trophy in front of a hometown crowd added a layer of meaning that few victories can match.

Joining an Elite Group of Champions

The US Open of Surfing is one of the sport's most prestigious and iconic events. With this victory, Marshall joins an elite group of Hurley athletes who have claimed the title, including two-time champions Brett Simpson, Filipe Toledo and Carissa Moore, as well as 2023 champion Eli Hanneman. Together, these victories reflect Hurley's longstanding legacy of supporting world-class athletes on surfing's biggest stages, a tradition that now includes Marshall's name among the sport's most accomplished competitors.

Hurley Leadership Reacts

"Jake has been part of Hurley since he was a grom, which makes watching him achieve this moment incredibly special for all of us," said Brett Simpson, Director of Sports Marketing at Hurley. "His talent has always been undeniable, but it is his character, determination and commitment to his craft that truly set him apart. We could not be prouder to celebrate this victory alongside Jake and everyone who has supported him throughout his journey."

A Career Built on Consistency and Connection

Marshall's US Open victory adds another milestone to a career shaped by fearless surfing, consistency and a deep connection to the Southern California surf community. His performance in Huntington Beach is a testament to the work that happens long before competition begins and to the belief required to rise when the pressure is at its highest. It is a result that will resonate with the next generation of young surfers watching from the beach, many of whom see in Marshall's journey a reflection of their own path from local breaks to the world stage.

Looking Ahead

Hurley congratulates Jake Marshall on an extraordinary achievement and a moment that will be remembered for years to come. As Marshall looks ahead to the next stages of his career, this victory stands as a defining chapter — one that cements his place among the sport's elite while inspiring the surfers who will follow in his footsteps.
excerpt: Jake Marshall claimed the 2026 US Open of Surfing title in Huntington Beach, defeating Kanoa Igarashi in the men's final with a heat score of 14.77, capping a career-defining performance in front of a hometown crowd and joining an elite group of Hurley champions.
